speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources whether the Ministry has been conducting audits on social enterprises managing hawker centres to prevent the use of hidden fees and charges and what level of surplus of income is deemed acceptable for these social enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: As private sector operators, they have experience in food and beverage operations as well as property and lease management.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This expertise could be harnessed to attract new hawkers to the trade, provide residents with a variety of good and affordable food choices, and improve the vibrancy of the hawker centres by, amongst others, ensuring that sufficient stalls are open during meal times and organising place-making programmes at the centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: This is in contrast to some existing hawker centres where stallholders operate shorter hours and, hence, do not fully cater to the dining needs of residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The operators have brought benefits to patrons and stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: They have ensured that hawkers provide clean and tasty meals to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The operators have also introduced interesting food concepts and options, such as prawn paste chicken rice and halal zichar, and new dining concepts, such as the "Fareground" at Pasir Ris Central hawker centre, which brings together "hipster" hawker fare, such as beef bourguignon and kebabs, to attract younger patrons to the hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The operators have also implemented productivity improvements that are critical for this manpower-intensive sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Centralised dishwashing has reduced hawkers' workload while improving the cleanliness of the centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: During my recent visit to Our Tampines Hub hawker centre, a stallholder expressed that centralised dishwashing helped him save on water charges and addressed his challenges of hiring dishwashers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The operators have also complemented the Government's efforts to support aspiring new hawkers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: One example is the Entrepreneurship Programme (EP) introduced by Fei Siong at Hougang Ci Yuan hawker centre, where new hawkers are provided with on-the-job training to help new entrants operate their stalls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: They are mentored by veteran hawkers, some of whom have even shared culinary experiences as well as their recipes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that there have been concerns over costs to stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: NEA ensures that rentals charged and essential services that contribute to operating costs are reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Operators who propose lower rentals and operating costs will be considered more favourably, and they are not permitted to vary these charges over the term of the tenancy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Before signing any tenancy agreement with potential stallholders, the operators will have to make known these charges to them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Operators must also bear the risks of rental arrears and stall vacancies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: In addition, NEA requires operators to be transparent about costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These measures limit the potential profits, if any, of operators and ensure that rentals are affordable for stallholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: Today, the stall rentals, together with operating costs, at our new hawker centres are significantly lower than those in comparable food courts and coffee shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The operators also fund their own initiatives to achieve social objectives and enhance the vibrancy of the hawker centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: These include the $1 Meal Carnival at Yishun Park hawker centre in June this year to attract the community to dine at the centre, and the offering of drinks at concessionary rates for senior citizens at Jurong West hawker centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: It takes time for a new hawker centre to establish itself.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: The Government will continue to refine and improve the management model, so as to provide affordable food in a hygienic environment while allowing hawkers to make a decent livelihood.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for the Environment and Water Resources (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources)
text: With time, we expect the new hawker centres to enhance their vibrancy and grow into valued community dining rooms.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Was NEA aware of the extra costs that were at the centre of the recent public concerns?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is, does NEA conduct regular surveys of hawkers with respect to satisfaction with management or any other management issues that they bring up to NEA?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think the operator had explained, had come out to clarify, and we have also made clarifications that the costs are optional costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted, all mandatory charges have to be declared upfront to the stallholders before they sign on the tenancy agreement.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, even though we have appointed operators to manage our new hawker centres, we also have place managers that visit the hawker centres regularly, on a weekly basis, to carry out checks on defects, on cleanliness as well as to engage the stallholders.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the stallholders can, at any time approach our place managers if there are pertinent issues.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have a follow up question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I agree with her that it takes time for the hawkers to establish themselves.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: But there are some that are still struggling among the hawker centres managed by the social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: So, I would like to ask whether NEA would consider lowering the rentals for a period of time until they could pick up enough business to make it sustainable?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have noted, for the new hawker centres, the rentals for the stalls as well as the operating costs for essential services – general cleaning, dishwashing and so on – are made known to the stallholders so you would assume that when they signed on the tenancy agreement, they would have taken into account all these costs in their computations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, even in our existing hawker centres which are tendered out, they would also have tendered based on what they understand to be the market rate, in most instances.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we do understand and appreciate the concerns of the stallholders and we are keeping a close watch on the situation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a matter of fact, for the new hawker centres, as I have said, it takes time for them to establish their business.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And I think it is not unexpected that some stalls may not do as well as others at the beginning.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The footfall for some of these hawker centres have increased over time significantly.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A quick point to echo what Member of Parliament Zainal Sapari has said whether we really can provide some subsidies for the hawkers at some of these social enterprise hawker centres who are really not doing well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I know they came in knowing what the rental is.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the fact now is that, in contrast to what Assoc Prof Daniel Goh had stated, some of them are really finding it hard to break even – the social enterprises.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, can we provide some help to the hawkers at these social enterprise hawker centres which really are not doing well because of very low footfall?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think that when there are specific cases, it can be made known to us.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have said, we keep a close watch on the viability of the businesses in these new hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And as of now, even for the hawker centres which had some bad press coverage and apparently low footfall, they have actually improved their business significantly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The operators have been able to enhance the vibrancy of these hawker centres, for instance, providing free shuttle bus service to the nearby industries and factories as well as office workers to dine in the hawker centres, complimentary car parking, as well as discounts, lucky draws and so on to bring them in.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, in Jurong West hawker centre, they have managed to bring in some popular stallholders which have also significantly increased the footfall.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, based on our understanding and survey of what is happening, we do not see that there is a need to do this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have said, if there are individual stalls that face problems, we can always take a look at it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: With regard to the social enterprises, are they sustainable?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: Because if they are facing problems in terms of keeping up with costs themselves and trying to get more money because, putting in all these extra costs to the hawkers, are they doing well?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think the earlier question was not about whether the social enterprise was doing well, but the particular individual stallholders, from Member of Parliament Louis Ng.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the social enterprise, as I have said, when they bid for the hawker centres, they know that we will consider favourably those where they offer lower rentals, lower operating costs and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They have to bear risks of rental arrears as well as vacancies and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, again the terms of the tenure are clear, transparent.
